fantasy: Reading the ice three slides ahead: once a penguin pushes off, nothing stops it but the world, so every choice is a commitment made in advance.
core_loop: Read the level -> pick a direction -> the penguin slides until it hits a wall, a door or the goal -> keys unlock their doors and crumbling tiles vanish behind you -> reach the goal inside the move budget for up to three stars -> the next level adds a rule (a key, a door, a crumbling tile) or tightens the budget.
pillars: A slide is fully readable before it is committed: the direction plus what sits in its path tells you exactly where the penguin stops
Nothing on the board moves except the penguin, and only on the player's input - a door opens or a tile crumbles only because the penguin crossed it
A level is solvable at a glance within its move cap and finished inside ninety seconds

engine.rationale: The play happens on a flat ice-grid plane: a sliding puzzle needs no depth to read, and 2D with vector art keeps the first load small on portal traffic, where time to first play decides whether the player stays.
engine.camera: Fixed, the board centred, no scrolling.

features.name: Ice board
features.description: A grid of ice tiles bounded by walls and rocks that a slide stops against.
acceptance: The board is between 6x6 and 9x9 depending on the level, and every cell is ice, wall, rock, or the goal.
Every authored board is solvable inside its move cap, and the level data stores that solution's length.
Strategy MVP: 6 designed levels with authored difficulty on depth, move-limit, board-complexity, piece-variety.

features.name: Directional slide
features.description: A tapped or swiped direction sends the penguin sliding cell by cell until it hits a wall, a rock, a closed door, or the board's edge.
acceptance: The penguin moves every open cell in the chosen direction and stops in the last cell before whatever blocks it.
A slide costs one move whether it travels one cell or the whole board.
Choosing a direction the penguin cannot move in (blocked on the very first cell) costs no move.

features.name: Goal tile
features.description: A marked exit tile; the penguin stopping on it clears the level.
acceptance: The penguin's slide ending exactly on the goal tile clears the level immediately.
The goal tile is visually distinct from ice, wall, rock, key, door and crumbling tiles at a glance.

features.name: Move budget and stars
features.description: Each level carries a par move count and a hard move cap; reaching the goal inside the cap wins, and how close to par decides one to three stars.
acceptance: Every slide decrements the level's moves-left counter by one.
Reaching the goal with moves-left at or above the level's 3-star threshold awards three stars; lower thresholds award two or one.
Moves-left reaching zero before the goal is reached fails the level and offers an immediate retry on the same board.
Strategy MVP: Core loop: read the level, plan the moves, solve it, advance to a harder level that adds a rule or tightens the budget.
Strategy MVP: The brief, built in full: A sliding-ice puzzle: a penguin slides until it hits something; 24 hand-designed levels with keys, doors, crumbling tiles and a 3-star move target.

features.name: Keys and doors
features.description: A key tile is collected the instant the penguin's slide crosses or stops on it; a door of the matching colour then opens and no longer blocks a slide.
acceptance: The penguin crossing or stopping on a key tile removes that key from the board and marks it collected in the HUD.
A door blocks a slide like a wall until its matching key is collected, after which it is open for the rest of the attempt.
A door with no matching key yet collected cannot be crossed or stopped on.

features.name: Crumbling tile
features.description: An ice tile that crumbles into a hole the instant the penguin's slide crosses it; a hole ends the attempt if the penguin crosses or stops on it again.
acceptance: The first time a slide passes over or stops on a crumbling tile, it turns into a hole for the rest of the attempt.
A slide that would cross or stop on a hole fails the level immediately, with an immediate retry offered.
A crumbling tile's crumbled (hole) state is visually unmistakable from its intact state.

progression: Linear levels: Available from the start -> Levels 1-6 teach directional sliding, the goal tile, the move budget and stars, then keys, doors and crumbling tiles; Clear level 6 -> Levels 7-12 combine keys, doors and crumbling tiles on bigger boards; Clear level 12 -> Levels 13-18 add double-key doors and three-key levels; Clear level 18 -> Levels 19-24 are four-key finales with every rule combined and the tightest budgets.
difficulty: Levels 1-2: An empty board and the goal tile only, six or more moves of slack; the level cannot realistically be failed. Levels 3-6: One key and door, then a crumbling tile, slack falling to four moves. Levels 7-10: Two keys, two doors and two crumbling tiles on a larger board, slack at three to four moves. Levels 11-18: A double-key door and up to three keys, slack falling to two moves. Levels 19-24: Four keys, two double-key doors and four crumbling tiles, slack falling to one move at the tightest; every fourth or fifth level is a breather with slack restored. Assist: After two failed attempts on one level, the next attempt starts with two extra moves and highlights one correct direction once.
controls: Slide up: Tap the up arrow docked above the board or swipe up (touch), W or Up arrow (keyboard). Slide down: Tap the down arrow or swipe down (touch), S or Down arrow (keyboard). Slide left: Tap the left arrow or swipe left (touch), A or Left arrow (keyboard). Slide right: Tap the right arrow or swipe right (touch), D or Right arrow (keyboard). Pause: Pause button (touch), Esc or P (keyboard).

ux.onboarding: Diegetic. The first board has exactly one open direction that reaches the goal, and its shape teaches the rule without a sentence.
ux.accessibility: Every audio cue has a visual counterpart, so the game plays muted - which also covers the large share of portal traffic that plays with sound off. Colour is never the only signal. Text is at least 16 CSS px at the design resolution. A reduced-motion setting (and prefers-reduced-motion) disables shake and flashes.

art_direction: Layered cut paper lit from one side, recoloured for an arctic diorama: soft depth, crisp edges, handmade warmth over ice blues and snow white. Identity kit 'paper-diorama-arctic'. Irregular cut-paper edges on panels, each layer casting a short hard shadow down-right; the penguin is a simple, rounded cut-paper character, not a tile.
audio_direction: Library music loop plus short library SFX, all compressed and loaded after first play so audio never delays time to first play. Every cue has a visual twin.

mastery.statement: A better player reads the whole level before the first slide - the walls, keys, doors and crumbling tiles already mapped - and commits to a short, exact sequence instead of feeling out the board one slide at a time.

meta_loop.statement: Clear a level -> earn its stars and open the next -> the star total opens the next level group -> come back for the stars left behind.

persists.what: Levels cleared and the level the player is on
Stars earned per level, out of three

goal_ladder.goal: Find the direction that gets the penguin a cell closer without wasting a move.
Clear this level with at least two stars.

content_schedule.name: Keys and doors
content_schedule.rule: A key opens its matching door; a door blocks a slide until that key is collected.

content_schedule.name: Crumbling tiles
content_schedule.rule: A crumbling tile turns into a hole the first time a slide crosses it; crossing the hole again ends the attempt.

content_schedule.name: Double-key doors
content_schedule.rule: A double-key door needs both of its matching keys collected before it opens.

content_schedule.name: Tight move budgets
content_schedule.rule: Move caps fall to within one or two moves of the clean solution.

first_session.ends_on: A cleared level with its stars stamped, and the next level's key-and-door count shown on the card.

return_hooks.statement: There is a next level and I can already see its board.
I left a star on level 12 and I already see the slide I should have made instead.

open_questions: The brief names no design archetype, so this design states the sliding-ice mechanic (slide until you hit a wall, key, door or crumbling tile) in full from the Level puzzle genre model's content rules. Confirm at G3 that this is the loop the brief meant.
A first-time player understands the tap control without instruction
The core loop produces an unforced desire to retry within one 300-second session
This risk is contained: Poki requires web exclusivity, so the candidate platforms cannot all be used for the same build; choosing is a strategy decision
The rewarded placement reads as a favour rather than an interruption
It holds 30 fps on a mid-range mobile browser inside a 100 MB bundle
